planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in spring in acid, moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil with afternoon shade; Cascade grows very slowly and its arching framework takes years to develop, so choose a permanent site with room for the branches to sweep low.

directions: Cascade is a distinctive semi-weeping selection with arching, pendulous branch tips that give the tree a fountain-like silhouette quite unlike the upright vase shape typical of the species, reaching only modest size even after decades in the landscape. White, gold-stamened, camellia-like flowers appear along the drooping branches in summer, followed by rich red-purple fall foliage and the mottled, exfoliating bark that defines the genus. Because growth is notably slow and the weeping form is most striking on a young, well-branched specimen, site it where it can be viewed up close as a garden focal point rather than massed with other trees, and keep the root zone consistently moist and undisturbed.

planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in spring in acid, moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil with afternoon shade; Korean Splendor establishes best when planted young, since stewartia resents root disturbance once settled.

directions: Korean Splendor is a vigorous selection of the Korean variety of Japanese stewartia, chosen for unusually large, wide-opening white flowers with prominent golden stamens that hold on the branches longer than typical seedling-grown trees. It combines this extended summer bloom with the variety's characteristically smooth, rounded, jigsaw-patterned exfoliating bark in gray, orange, and cream, plus reliable yellow-to-red-orange fall color that develops even in warmer parts of its range. Grow in consistently moist, acidic, well-drained soil with morning sun and afternoon shade, and avoid low or poorly drained sites, since prolonged wet soil in winter can be as damaging as summer drought.
